content.text:
Your query syntax is correct — `has` works the same nested inside a relation filter as it does on a top-level field (Prisma ORM v6 docs, `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v6/prisma-client/queries/filtering-and-sorting.mdx`, "Filter on scalar lists / arrays"). Nesting `company: { parking: { has: ... } }` inside your `Job.findMany` where is fine — no special syntax is needed for filtering scalar-list fields through a `-to-one` relation.

The likely real issue: scalar list filters (`has`, `hasEvery`, `hasSome`, `isEmpty`) are **only supported on PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, and MongoDB** (`apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/prisma-client/special-fields-and-types/working-with-scalar-lists-arrays.mdx`, "Filtering scalar lists"). If your Company table is on MySQL/SQL Server/SQLite, `has` won't work there at all — you'd need a join table instead of a native array.

Nesting `company: { parking: { has: ... } }` inside your `Job.findMany` where is fine — no special syntax is needed for filtering scalar-list fields through a `-to-one` relation.
